description: Compute FIRST and FOLLOW sets via fixed-point iteration over a right-recursive expression grammar.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `compute_first(grammar)` initializes each nonterminal's FIRST set to `set()` and repeats a `while changed:` loop until no new symbols are added. For each production `prod`, it walks symbols left to right. A terminal adds itself and breaks (lines 31-36). A nonterminal `sym` adds `first[sym] - {EPSILON}` and continues only if `EPSILON in first[sym]` (lines 38-44).

Look at the `for sym in prod: ... else:` block on lines 30-49. The `else` branch runs only if every symbol in `prod` can derive `EPSILON` without hitting `break`. This is the exact condition for adding `EPSILON` to `first[nt]`.
`first_of_string(symbols, first_sets, grammar_nts)` applies the same left-to-right rule to any slice of symbols (such as the suffix `beta` after a nonterminal in a production).

`compute_follow(grammar, first)` seeds `follow[start]` with `EOF` (`'$'`) on line 74, then scans every nonterminal occurrence `sym` at index `i` in `prod`. It adds `first_beta - {EPSILON}` (from `beta = prod[i+1:]`) to `follow[sym]`, and when `EPSILON in first_beta` (line 94), it also propagates `follow[nt]` into `follow[sym]`.
Lines 109-115 define the LL(1) expression grammar (`E`, `E'`, `T`, `T'`, `F`), and lines 117-129 compute and print the FIRST and FOLLOW sets for all five nonterminals.

steps.answer: All three have the exact same set, `{ '(', 'num' }`. `T -> F T'` starts with `F`, `E -> T E'` starts with `T`, and `F` never derives `EPSILON`.
steps.question: In `grammar` on lines 109-115, `F` starts with `'('` or `'num'`, and neither `F` nor `T` has an `EPSILON` production. What will `compute_first` produce for `FIRST(F)`, `FIRST(T)`, and `FIRST(E)`?

steps.description: Inside `compute_first`, once `first['F']` contains `'('` and `'num'`, line 41 propagates `new = first['F'] - {EPSILON}` into `first['T']`. It sets `changed = True` for the next pass.

title: Computing FIRST and FOLLOW Sets for an LL(1) Grammar
